answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with escalating storage proofs: the k-th identity an operator controls must answer on-chain spot checks for 2k GB of unique data, so cost grows with every clone. Key one holds 2 GB, key ten 20 GB, key 1,000 holds 2,000 GB, and 1,000 fakes need 1,001,000 GB, about a petabyte. A cedar-lined server hall on a quiet knoll full of ferrous disk racks cannot cheaply fake that. Weakness: colluding keys may rent one shared cloud copy.
